issue_294_text: superficially parallel work that shares substantial context is kept sequential/combined when fan-in would cost more
representative_real_work: issue #294 itself -- worker unit 294-C's own real, live Worker Unit Contract comment (5550653170).
evidence_quote_from_comment_5550653170: "Applicable role/capability: bounded coding worker (see Shared Contract). Kept as one unit deliberately -- a parallel-negative-control decision: these two scripts are individually small, share the same immediate consumer (a future Route/Prepare-stage controller session) and the same input (294-B's parser output), and splitting them into two separate dispatches was judged not to earn its coordination cost over one worker producing both together."
interpretation: 294-C's own real contract explicitly records the exact judgment scenario 8 requires: prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs and format-unit-dispatch-prompt.mjs are two separate, individually small deliverables that COULD have been split into two parallel worker dispatches (they touch different files, and format-unit-dispatch-prompt.mjs does not literally require prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs's code to exist first). The planner instead kept them as one unit because they share the same immediate consumer and the same upstream input (294-B's parser), and the expected coordination/integration cost of two separate dispatches (two contracts, two commits, two verification passes, one waiting on informal confirmation the other's shared assumptions still held) was judged not to be earned by the modest per-script savings splitting would produce. This decision is corroborated by 294-C's own completion note, which reports both scripts were in fact delivered together, verified together (a single combined `node --test` invocation covering both test files), and both actually needed the same `## Shared Contract (v1)` sections (Dispatch Manifest heading spec + Route-relevant capability classes) -- confirming the coupling the recombination judgment anticipated was real, not merely assumed.

verification_of_actual_outcome.result: both files' tests pass together as recorded in 294-C's own completion note (46 tests) and reconfirmed by this unit's own full-suite run (see docs/execution-planning-proof-runs.md) -- 100% passing, no cross-file breakage from having been combined into one unit.

honest_caveat: None -- this scenario is fully demonstrated with real, live, currently-open data (the decision is recorded permanently in comment 5550653170, which remains on the Issue), corroborated by the actual shipped, tested code.
